manifest.inventoryMeaning: Tracked *_test.go files, not test functions, cases, executed tests, or a coverage denominator.

review.rustIdentity: Exact cited file SHA256 values identify the inspected bytes, including shared-worktree changes. HEAD alone is not the complete working-tree identity.
review.method: Read fixed Go test bodies and current Rust assertion bodies; record scenario correspondence and missing branches. No cargo, Go test, game, user-computer access, fixture duplication, or product-code changes.
review.executionBlocker: Parent reports current Rust product-test execution blocked pending dependency/custody preparation; this mapping does not validate or clear that blocker.
review.staticValidation: Every Go test reference resolves at the fixed commit and matches inventory bytes/SHA256. Every Rust reference resolves to an existing #[test] function and records inspected file SHA256. URL commit/path/line anchors are generated from those local Git objects; no HTTP availability claim.

stateDefinitions.mapped-unrun: Named invariant/subscenario has corresponding assertions after body review; no execution or full-function/command equivalence claim.
stateDefinitions.partial: Related assertions exist, but specified cases/assertions/layers differ or a possible mismatch remains; no behavior pass.
stateDefinitions.uncovered: No corresponding assertion set established within this review scope; remaining repository may contain candidates.
stateDefinitions.not-applicable-with-specific-reason: Only for a documented implementation-specific mechanism whose business invariant is independently mapped elsewhere; none excluded in this initial map.

claimLimits: This is a bounded initial mapping for recent CLI and product/selection changes plus explicit high-priority follow-on cases, not a full audit of 359 files.
No behavioral-pass state is allowed. Rust function names, file counts, static catalog equality, compilation, and historical test records do not establish parity.
States apply to the written scenario scope. Multiple rows can reference one Go function, and one Rust function can support multiple rows; row totals are not coverage percentages.
No Go test or fixture is marked obsolete solely because Rust uses ownership, a different Source engine, or a newer protocol. No test has been deleted or copied by this change.
Platform-specific Go and Rust tests still require appropriate offline/automated Windows execution; Windows-specific is not game-dependent.
Both public output and side effects require paired differential evidence. All gaps remain open until such evidence exists.
